current: qip_edge::Cell::on_bytes and Cell::work touch memory and arithmetic only (module doc backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/lib.rs:16-19; grep finds no std::net/std::fs/TcpStream in cell.rs). gap: No dedicated test drives the requirement's own verification method: black-holing the Fabric/centre/model endpoints and a peer, then replaying a simulated venue event and asserting unchanged decision latency and an unchanged order. The invariant is proven today by code inspection (no I/O in the hot functions) plus adjacent tests (no-LLM reachability, mesh dead-letter/circuit-breaker), not by one test exercising this exact chaos scenario. qip-edge's own crate-level dependency graph does include qip-transport (for the separate, non-hot-path mesh module), so a naive crate-reachability architecture test of the kind the verification method describes would not by itself prove the invariant; it would need to be scoped to the on_bytes/work call graph. And the node binary links qip-storage (with a GCS client, for the journal mirror) as well as qip-transport, so the crate-level 'no network client on the tick-to-order path' assertion would fail today unless scoped to the Cell::on_bytes/work call graph.

current: qip_edge::envelope::VerifiedEnvelope and qip_edge::policy::{VerifiedPolicy, VerifiedHalt} verify an HMAC-SHA256 (qip_core::hmac_sha256, ADR 0002's named in-tree hashing) under a symmetric key the cell shares with the centre — the same refuse-on-tamper/refuse-on-missing-signature shape the requirement asks for, but with a shared secret rather than a KMS asymmetric signature.
gap: No KMS asymmetric signature verification exists or can exist in-tree today: it needs an asymmetric primitive (ADR 0043 names this as one of three gaps no in-tree code may close) and the Google auth flow a KMS call needs, which ADR 0009 forbids writing in-tree. A shared symmetric key is a weaker trust boundary than the requirement's threat model (anyone who can write to the package's storage cannot be distinguished from KMS by a shared secret two parties both hold).
verification: backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/tests/cell.rs's four signature tests prove the permitted (HMAC) form's refusal behaviour today. The requirement's own four-refusal integration check (flipped byte, digest mismatch, unknown key, no signature) is satisfied for HMAC, not for KMS.
notes: Recorded in ADR 0099's conflict register C2 as needing a dependency record (an asymmetric-primitive class) weighed against the in-tree-only policy before this can move.

current: Outcomes do reach the central ledger, though not from the journal and not through a Fabric. Each exchange publishes a CellStateDelta whose orders, fills, refusals and crosses are incremental since the previous delta (qip-edge/src/mesh.rs:179-236), idempotent by the cell's own sequence. qip-api drains the delta inbox into Platform::ingest_cell_report on POST /cycle (qip-api/src/mesh.rs:1621), which settles reported fills into the centre's strategy books. The hash-chained journal itself goes only to the node's configured KeyValueStore via Cell::flush (StoreMirror), and nothing central reads it back.
evidence: backend/crates/edge/qip-edge/src/mesh.rs:33-41 (nothing on the uplink is spooled; the incremental half of a delta whose circuit is open is lost)
backend/crates/apps/qip-api/src/mesh.rs:1-40,1621 (MeshBackbone drains deltas into ingest_cell_report), opened from qip-api/src/main.rs:318-320
backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/mirror.rs:1-50,183 (journal batches go to a KeyValueStore; `batches` is the only reader, in the node crate)
gap: What reaches the centre is a per-exchange delta, not the journal's records: it is not spooled, so the incremental orders/fills/refusals of any interval whose publish is dead-lettered or circuit-broken are lost (mesh.rs:33-41), which fails the requirement's 'every record reaches the Fabric exactly once after an outage'. Telemetry and policy/model acknowledgements do not travel at all. The drain is a blocking call on the pass thread, not asynchronous. There is no Fabric and no path from it to the learning loop.
verification: qip-api/tests/mesh.rs proves fills a cell reports over a real CellUplink reach the centre's books and that a redelivered delta is ingested once. Needed: journal-driven drain through the Fabric with an outage-and-restore session proving every outcome, telemetry and acknowledgement record arrives once, in journal order, with no decision waiting.
notes: Directly downstream of REFLEX-011; cannot be built before an embedded Fabric client exists to drain into. verify: upgraded MISSING -> PARTIAL with implemented/tested/integrated true. current: qip_contracts::message::MarketMessage carries two distinct required timestamp fields — venue_time ('when the venue says it happened') and capture_time ('when this cell's hardware saw the packet') — with a transit() method computing wire latency between them. qip-protocols' FIX/ITCH/SBE decoders (tested, unwired) set these from genuinely distinct sources.
evidence: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/feed.rs:425-426 (DepthDecoder passes the same `captured_at` value for both venue_time and capture_time)
gap: The one decoder actually reached from a composition root (DepthDecoder, for the simulated feed) sets venue_time = capture_time — the same value — because the simulator supplies no independent source timestamp, so in the only running configuration the two fields never diverge and REFLEX-019's specific purpose (measuring market-event-to-decision latency, and knowing what the node knew and when) is not exercised end-to-end. Also, capture_time is the probe instant (clock.now() once per health-probe iteration, main.rs:811) stamped on every line of the frame, not a per-message receipt time, and it comes from SystemClock (wall clock), so nothing guarantees or tests monotonicity within an adapter.
verification: backend/crates/edge/qip-protocols/tests/itch.rs and framing.rs prove venue_time/capture_time distinctness for the unwired decoders; no test proves it for the production-reached DepthDecoder because that decoder cannot distinguish them by construction.
notes: Cheap partial fix available even before REFLEX-016 closes: give the simulated feed its own independent 'venue-side' clock so the two fields genuinely diverge in the one path that runs today. verify: kept PARTIAL. Added that the receipt stamp is one wall-clock instant per probe, not per message, and that no test asserts per-adapter monotonicity.
